items.text: MQTT · one connection, several live readings
Start node tools/serve-mqtt-example.cjs, then click Apply / Connect. JSON drives the Gauge; the text topic drives the label and event log.

Retained / initial readings establish a value without appending to the log. Later live messages append once, including equal text. Disconnect makes the reading unavailable; its timestamp and stale status remain visible.
Another sketch · the same MQTT Config
This workspace uses Whole workspace execution. The connection on the first sketch stays active while this view subscribes through the same Config.

Try it
• Connect on the first sketch, then switch between the two views. They share one broker connection.
• Stop and restart the example server: the Config shows reconnecting, then subscriptions recover.
• Disconnect explicitly: it stays disconnected until Apply / Connect.
• In the editor, Subscribe → Edit lets you choose an MQTT Config by sketch and instance name.

Defaults
Manual connection. No credentials saved unless explicitly included in an export. Initial / retained messages never emit actions. Pause or hiding the browser suspends connections; resuming reconnects. In Active sketch mode, leaving a sketch disconnects its Config and returning requires Connect. The third sketch sends explicit commands through this same Config.
Commands & replies · broker receipt and device response
Connect the Local demo broker on the first sketch. Choose a value, then click Send. Changing the slider only prepares the JSON; it never sends a command by itself.

Each Send captures the topic and payload.
No queue while disconnected; reconnect never replays a command.

QoS 1 confirms broker receipt, not device execution. This local demo simulates a device response on a separate topic after a short delay. Retain is off for commands; a retained reply supplies the initial display without adding a log entry. Try sending the same value twice.
